body.title: Stop review guidance from prompting sleep-based waits
body.reproduction: Start a design review or a code review from a Claude Code session and follow the shipped review guidance while it runs. The design-review guidance says to poll `progress` "about every 10–30 seconds" [[c1]] [[c3]]; the code-review steps say to observe progress but give no rule for how to wait between calls [[c2]]. Claude Code refuses a foreground `sleep 45` and tells the agent to "use Monitor with an until-loop" [[c4]]. Observed in session 1ba9ad48 (both times while polling a code review): on 2026-11-13 at 05:32 UTC the agent started a background `until grep -q … /dev/null; do sleep 20; done &` loop labelled "Placeholder no-op" that can never finish (it ran about 32 hours until killed) and a 10-minute Monitor that only sleeps; on 2026-11-14 at 12:57 UTC it armed another 10-minute Monitor described as "placeholder" that only sleeps [[c4]]. Each time it then kept calling `progress` every few seconds anyway. In the VS Code chat the session stays held while such a wait is armed, so the user's next message queued for up to ten minutes while the chat showed idle. Expected: the agent waits for a review without inventing waits that do nothing, and never leaves one armed when it hands control back to the user.
body.rootCause: The review guidance asks for a polling interval but says nothing about how to wait for it, and the only interval it names is a fixed sleep the agent's harness forbids [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c3]]. Told to space its polls and refused a plain sleep, the agent satisfies the harness's suggestion with a Monitor or background loop that has no real condition [[c4]]. Nothing in the guidance says such a wait must watch something real, must end when the review ends, or must be stopped before the turn ends.
body.fixIntent: Reword the waiting guidance in both review sections of the steering block and in the design-review execution document. The agent should either call `progress` again directly, without sleeping between calls, or wait with one background command whose own exit is the review reaching a terminal status in its checkpoint. It must never arm a placeholder or no-op wait (a loop or monitor with no real condition), and it must stop any wait it armed before ending a turn that asks the user a question. Guidance text only: no code, tool or schema change; the VS Code plugin picks the steering text up at its next packaging.
